scope: Native Mac Month-grid keyboard navigation in isolated grammar workspace; iOS receives status/evidence only.
initialGap: Clicking 11 November followed by Right Arrow paged to December and selected December 1. Date cells had no date-level keyboard navigation.
implementation: Month cells own focused-date state, selected trait, complete date/task-count label and explicit primary/Open day actions.
Down from calendar focus enters date navigation; Left/Right move one day and Up/Down one week.
Return opens the exact selected day; Escape explicitly restores period navigation.
Calendar-level handling covers native collection focus; period changes request focus after the old cell is recreated.
Command, Option, Control and Shift combinations are ignored; platform arrow-key flags do not reject ordinary arrows.
intermediateFindings: First handler rejected platform arrow-key flags.
Changing a button into a focused cell required applying its semantic labels after accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).
Collection focus needed calendar-level date handling.
Recreating the month grid lost focus; explicit deferred calendar refocus preserves boundary movement.
Escape required a new focus request even when the parent binding still read true.
limits: Final native acceptance is scoped to the named normal/light wide-window workflow.
Compact pointer routing, Year-grid keyboard, actual VoiceOver, iOS/iPad hardware keyboard and broader accessibility acceptance remain open.
No sync/data-contract changes or iOS production changes. No new Mac XCTest runtime pass.
